Does the self-report track the internal emotion vector? — gemma-4-31b-it (base)

Isaac’s question, on the existing probe data: 4 experiments separating "report reflects internal state" from "report just echoes the scenario text".

Config / setup
Modelgemma-4-31b-it (base)
Transcriptselicitation feel + rate · all scenarios × 8 framings × n=10 · coherent+disclosed only
n (gated)rate 3799 · feel 2753
Probecosine of each token’s residual onto the per-layer emotion direction, averaged over the user-prompt tokens (scenario + question; the model’s reply is excluded). Every framing is a single user+model exchange except ICL, which prepends few-shot example turns — there we take the final/real user query. Then z-scored per (layer,emotion)
Self-reportrate = model’s 1-5 PANAS ratings (code-parsed); feel = Opus-4.8 0-10 levels; z-scored per emotion
Layerbest layer per experiment (where probe best recovers the scenario emotion): rate L33, feel L33

Metrics — what each experiment measures

expquestionmetric (how computed)
E1 validitydoes the emotion vector fire for the right scenario?confusion of probe-argmax (internal) vs scenario emotion; diagonal rate (chance 12.5%). Probe = code/cosine, no judge.
E2 overalldoes the report align with the probe at all?Pearson corr of the report 8-vector vs the probe 8-vector, pooled over transcript×emotion. CONFOUNDED: both are driven by the scenario.
E3 text-controlleddoes the report track the probe BEYOND the text?same correlation after subtracting each scenario’s mean from both (partial corr controlling scenario). win>0 = alignment survives with the text held fixed.
E4 off-scriptwhen the report leaves the obvious answer, is it internally grounded?restrict to transcripts where report-argmax ≠ scenario; fraction where probe-argmax = report vs = scenario (chance 1/7).

z-score (per emotion) = normalization. Yes — for each emotion we subtract its average activation over ALL transcripts and divide by its standard deviation, so the value becomes "how many SDs above/below that emotion's own average" (0 = average, +1 = one SD above, −1 = one SD below). Why: the raw cosines have very different baselines per emotion (some directions read high for every transcript), which would swamp the comparison; z-scoring puts all 8 emotions on the same footing so "anger is elevated here" means elevated relative to anger's usual level, and the 8 are comparable to each other.

ResultsMethods
Bottom line — Isaac's question
  • E1: the emotion vectors do fire for the right scenario on the user prompt (target is the top bar in 5/8 rate, 3/8 feel; per-transcript argmax 41%/41% vs 12.5% chance) — real but noisy.
  • E3: once the scenario is held fixed the report↔probe correlation is weak for both modalities (rate 0.34→0.14, feel 0.38→0.14) — most of the raw alignment was just the shared scenario.
  • E4 is where the modalities split: when the model reports an emotion the scenario did NOT script, the probe backs the report for feel (29% vs 17% scenario) but backs the scenario for rate (32% vs 15% report ≈ chance). So feel's off-script reports are internally grounded; rate's look like noise.
  • Caveat: the probe is a weak instrument (E1 ~41% recovers the scenario), so these are modest effects, not slam-dunks; the cleaner test is steer-and-ask (no scenario at all).

E1 · is E's vector highest on E's scenarios? (Roleplay framing)

Q: during E's ROLEPLAY scenarios, probing the USER PROMPT, is E's emotion vector high vs the other 7?

Setup. Filtered to the roleplay framing only. Probe each transcript on the user-prompt tokens (scenario + question; the model's reply is excluded), mean-pooled, z-scored per emotion. For each scenario emotion we plot the mean probe activation of all 8 emotions (target highlighted). Tokens probed: the user prompt (scenario + question), mean-pooled. The feel experiment is collapsed below (rate is the focus for now).

▸ feel experiment (same plot, collapsed)
Result
  • Plotted: each bar = the mean z-scored probe activation of one emotion on this scenario's roleplay user prompts. z-score = (token cosine − that emotion's mean over ALL transcripts) / its SD, so 0 = the emotion's baseline, positive = above. Computed by projecting each user-prompt token's residual onto that emotion's layer-L direction (cosine), averaging over the user-prompt tokens, then z-scoring per emotion.
  • Roleplay only: the target emotion's vector is the tallest bar in 4/8 scenario-emotions (rate, n=480 transcripts; feel 5/8).
  • Anger and fear still tend to lose to their near-synonyms (frustration / anxiety) — the same confusion the self-reports show.
Example transcripts — per-token emotion activation (centered across all emotions & transcripts)

Pick an experiment + scenario emotion — one transcript each for the baseline, roleplay, minsys, prefill framings is shown stacked. Each token of the full transcript (user prompt + model response) is heat-colored by its probe activation, double-centered (minus the emotion's global baseline across all transcripts, and minus the token's mean over emotions) — same scheme as the on-policy movie. Each token is colored for the selected emotion: red = above that emotion's baseline, blue = below. Hover a token for its top emotions.

E2 · probe at the RATING-NUMBER token vs self-rating (roleplay, rate)

Q: when the model writes its 1-5 rating for emotion E, is E's vector active at that number token — and does it match the rating it wrote?

Setup. Roleplay framing, rate experiment. In each model RESPONSE we locate each emotion's rating-number token (the digit in 'emotion: N') and probe the residual there onto that emotion's layer-L direction (cosine). Per scenario (8 subplots), per emotion: two side-by-side bars on the same z-scale — green = probe-z at the rating token, blue = the self-rating (also z-scored per emotion; the raw 1-5 is the number label on the blue bar). Matching bar heights = the internal signal tracks the rating. Tokens probed: the rating-number token in the response, layer L33. Both bars are z-scored (SDs above/below that emotion's average) so they're directly comparable.

Result
  • Read per emotion within each scenario: green (probe-z at the moment the number is written) rising together with blue (the number itself) = the internal signal matches the rating the model wrote.
  • Context (user-prompt readout, all framings pooled): overall corr(report, probe) 0.34 rate / 0.38 feel; probe-argmax = report-argmax 32% / 46% (chance 12.5%).

E3 · text-controlled alignment

Q: does the report track the probe when the scenario text is held fixed?

Setup. Repeat the E2 correlation within each of the 48 scenarios (subtract each scenario's mean from both probe and report), so the text is partialled out. Grey = raw; green = within-scenario. Tokens probed: user-prompt tokens (scenario + question), mean-pooled, z-scored per emotion (same readout as E1).

Result
  • rate: drops from 0.34 to 0.14 — most of the raw alignment was the shared scenario; within a fixed scenario the linear report↔probe correlation is weak.
  • feel: also drops to 0.14 (from 0.38). Within a fixed scenario the correlation is weak for both modalities; what separates them is the argmax / off-script behavior in E4, not this correlation.

E4 · off-script reports

Q: when the model reports an emotion the scenario did NOT script, does the internal probe back the report or the scenario?

Setup. Restrict to transcripts where the report's top emotion differs from the scenario's, then ask whether the probe's top emotion equals the report or the scenario (chance 1/7). Tokens probed: user-prompt tokens (scenario + question), mean-pooled, z-scored per emotion (same readout as E1).

Result
  • rate (n=1972): the probe backs the scenario (32%) over the report (15%≈chance) — those deviations look like noise, not introspection.
  • feel (n=1189): the probe backs the report (29%) over the scenario (17%) — the off-script reports are internally grounded.

Replication

  1. Probe (already run): ops/emotion_probe.py over feel + rate shards → probe/{feel,rate}/<Emotion>.npz = per-token × 60-layer × 8-emotion cosine onto the per-layer directions (perlayer_matrix.npz).
  2. This analysis: ops/probe_report_align.py. Probe vector per transcript = mean over PROMPT tokens (tokens before the gemma model turn), z-scored per (layer,emotion). Report vector = parsed 1-5 ratings (rate) or Opus levels (feel), z-scored per emotion. Best layer = argmax over layers of probe-argmax==scenario.
  3. E1 confusion(scenario, probe-argmax). E2 Pearson over flattened transcript×emotion. E3 subtract each scenario’s per-emotion mean from probe and report, then the same Pearson (partial corr controlling scenario). E4 mask report-argmax≠scenario; fractions probe==report / probe==scenario.
  4. Gating: coherent+disclosed only (rate via rate_disclosure.json; feel via emolevel reports_feeling+coherent). 95% CI on correlations via Fisher z.

Note: the probe is a weak instrument here (E1 diagonal well below 1), and on naturalistic scenarios internal state and surface text are largely confounded — E3/E4 are the parts that try to separate them.
